SEARCH

All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
AimJitter
SHIELD-2: an aim offset a bullet shielder can't predict, small enough to stay on its body.
Angles
Angle normalisation, bit-for-bit identical to robocode.util.Utils so the core behaves exactly as it did when it called the engine's helpers.
AntiSurferFormula
The anti-surfer views' feature space: the first nine features of GunFormula, computed the same way, without the melee crowd feature.
AntiSurferGun
The anti-surfer gun: four small, fast-forgetting KNN views whose neighbours are pooled and scored on a fixed grid of firing angles.
BattleField
The battle field's walls, as seen by a robot's centre, and the geometry that depends on them: clamping a point into the field, how far a target can move before a wall stops it (two of the gun's and the surf's KNN features), and wall smoothing.
BattleResult
One battle's outcome from Hadur's point of view, as a CSV row.
BattleRunner
Runs one battle in this JVM and writes result.csv into the battle directory.
Bench
Runs Hadur against the reference set and writes a score-share report.
BotEvent
Engine events delivered to the robot during a tick, as plain immutable values.
BotEvent.BulletHit
One of our bullets hit name, leaving it with energy.
BotEvent.BulletHitBullet
One of our bullets collided with an enemy bullet, which was at x, y.
BotEvent.BulletMissed
One of our bullets left the field; bulletHeading as for BotEvent.BulletHit.
BotEvent.HitByBullet
An enemy bullet hit us.
BotEvent.HitRobot
We collided with another robot.
BotEvent.HitWall
We drove into a wall.
BotEvent.RobotDeath
A robot died.
BotEvent.Scan
The radar saw a robot.
BotEvent.SkippedTurn
The engine skipped one of our turns because the previous tick ran too long.
BotEvent.TickTime
How long the core's previous tick took, measured by the adapter, and the allowance it assumes per turn (TIME-1).
BotInput
Everything the core sees in one tick: the robot's own state and the events that arrived with it.
BotOrders
What the robot should do this tick.
BotOrders.Builder
Collects orders as the core decides them; later calls in a tick win, like Robocode setters.
BulletShadows
MOVE-1: where our bullets shadow an enemy wave.
Bytes
Big-endian byte writing and reading for the profile format, without java.io (the core does no I/O, RES-6).
Bytes.Reader
Reads big-endian values from buf[start, end).
Bytes.Writer
A growable big-endian byte buffer.
DiaUtils
Small geometry and arithmetic helpers shared by the whole core: projecting points, bearings between points, bullet flight times, the orbit's acceleration sign, firing-angle grids and a Wald margin of error.
DistanceFormula
Turns a Wave into a point in a KNN feature space, and says how much each axis of that space counts.
DistancePolicy
The distance Hadur tries to fight at (the artifact's distance controller). 1.20 held a fixed 650 px, which on an 800x600 field is a retreat: bullets take 33-45 ticks to arrive and our own gun's escape angle is at its widest.
DistancePolicy.Step
How a wave moved the target: IN a step on a certain lead of ours, OUT a step on their lead, or HOLD with no clear lead either way, no rates yet, or the target already at the bound it would move toward.
DuelFocus
The one opponent the duel fights while several are alive and melee is vetoed (GATE-3, GATE-4): the closest when the duel takes over, kept until it dies, so the duel's model of its enemy is always about one robot.
Endgame
The two endgame states.
Endgame.State
The endgame state for one tick.
EnemyGunHeat
The enemy's gun heat as far as its shots show it (END-1 compares it with ours).
EnemyInfo
Latest known state of one opponent in the current round.
EnemyShot
A shot an opponent fired, inferred from an energy drop the core could not explain as damage (MSENSE-2): who fired, from where, when, and at what power.
EnemyTracker
Per-round model of the battlefield: every opponent Hadur has scanned, its last position, heading, velocity, energy and scan tick, whether it is alive, and the shots its energy drops show (MSENSE-2).
EnergyLedger
Explains the enemy's energy changes between two scans, so that only a drop the enemy spent on a bullet becomes a wave (WAVE-1, WAVE-2).
EnergyLedger.Reading
One scan's reading.
Estimate
A rate and its 95% margin of error (DIAL-1): every input the opening book reads carries both, so a policy can tell "their gun hits 15% of the time" from "it hit 1 of 6 shots".
FileProfileStore
The ProfileStore on Robocode's data directory.
FileProfileStore.Opener
Opens a file for writing; the robot uses Robocode's stream, tests a plain one.
FlattenerFormula
The flattener's feature space: MoveFormula's nine attributes of our movement when an enemy wave was fired, plus our displacement over the last 20 and 40 ticks, with its own weights.
Guard
Makes sure the robot gets orders every tick (RES-1).
GunController
The duel's gun: owns every opponent's gun views, picks which gun aims, scores the virtual guns, learns from each gun wave as it breaks, and chooses the bullet power.
GunController.Opening
The gun an opening book asks for until the live virtual guns clearly disagree (ADAPT-1).
GunFormula
The main gun's feature space: ten features of the target's situation when a gun wave was fired, each scaled to about [0, 1].
Hadur
The Robocode adapter.
HadurCore
Hadur's brain.
HadurRecorder
Hadur, plus a transcript of every input and order in Replay's format.
HitWindow
A rolling hit rate: the last capacity shot outcomes and their estimate (DIST-1's "rolling hit rate").
KdTree<T>
Weighted squared-Euclidean KD-tree with optional FIFO size limit.
KdTree.Entry<T>
One search result.
KnnView<T>
One KNN "view" of an opponent: a feature space (its DistanceFormula), a bounded KdTree of past wave outcomes in that space, and the settings that say which waves it learns from and how many neighbours it returns.
LineageKey
Turns the name the radar reports into the key a profile is filed under, so that every version of a robot shares one profile: "abc.Shadow 3.84" and "abc.Shadow 3.83c (2)" are both "abc.Shadow".
LineCodec
Text form of BotInput and BotOrders, one line each, so a battle can be recorded and replayed through the core (CORE-2).
LogHarvester
Collects what a battle looked like from the outside.
MainGun
The main gun: a KNN displacement-vector gun with a kernel-density choice of angle.
MaxEscapeTarget
The result of a precise maximum-escape-angle prediction: how far, as an angle seen from a wave's source, the target can get from its bearing at fire time before the wave reaches it, and where it would be then.
MeleeController
Runs Hadur's melee subsystems for one tick and returns what the robot should do.
MeleeController.Command
What Hadur should do this tick.
MeleeController.Situation
What Hadur knows about itself this tick.
MeleeGun
Melee targeting: circular prediction, falling back to linear prediction when the opponent's turn rate is unknown.
MeleeGun.Aim
 
MeleeGun.Strategy
 
MeleeHarvester
Watches a melee battle from the outside, for the melee gates.
MeleeRadar
Melee radar.
MeleeReport
The melee bench's report, built from each battle's melee.csv (the engine's final scores), rounds.csv (MeleeHarvester) and hadur.log.
MeleeReport.Battle
One battle's outcome.
MeleeRunner
Runs one melee battle in this JVM and writes melee.csv into the battle directory: one row per robot in finishing order.
MeleeStrategy
Picks Hadur's overall posture in a melee from the state of the battle.
MeleeStrategy.Plan
The chosen posture, plus what it implies for targeting and positioning.
MeleeStrategy.Posture
 
MeleeTargetSelector
Chooses which opponent to shoot at in a melee.
MemoryProfileStore
A ProfileStore held in memory, for tests and the bench.
MemoryProfileStore.Crash
Thrown by a write that MemoryProfileStore.crashAfter(int) cut short.
MinimumRiskMovement
Melee movement: minimum risk (MMOVE-1..4), the HawkOnFire and Diamond shape.
MinimumRiskMovement.View
What the movement sees this tick.
MoveController
What the duel's surf knows about the enemy's gun: its waves in flight, the KNN danger views that score where on a wave its bullets go, its hit rate on us, and our bullets in flight with the shadows they cast on its waves (MOVE-1).
MoveFlavour
MOVE-2: when the enemy hits us more than its profile says it does, beyond the margin of error, the movement changes flavour at the next surfable wave.
MoveFlavour.Step
The flavours in the order they are added; each keeps the ones before it.
MoveFormula
The surf's main feature space: nine attributes of our own movement when an enemy wave was fired, each scaled to about [0, 1], that the danger views' KD-trees search for the enemy's past firing situations most like the one being surfed.
MovementPredictor
Tick-by-tick prediction of a robot's movement under Robocode's physics, and the precise maximum escape angle built on it.
Opening
What the opening book decided for one battle, read once from the profile at the first scan (the artifact's "one struct").
Opening.Gun
The gun to start with (ADAPT-1), from the movement tier.
OpeningBook
Reads a profile's tiers once and turns them into an Opening (the artifact's "Recognise, then adapt").
Opponent
One entry of reference-set.txt.
OpponentProfile
Everything Hadur remembers about one opponent lineage between battles (the artifact's profile schema): who it is, how recent battles went, how its gun does against us, how it moves under our guns, and seed samples for the KNN views (S4).
OpponentProfile.BattleOutcome
One battle's result as Hadur saw it.
OpponentStats
Statistics about one opponent, accumulated across every round of a battle.
OpponentStats.GunType
 
OpponentStats.MovementType
 
OpponentStatsBook
Battle-long store of OpponentStats.
OurBullet
One of our bullets in flight, as the core fired it: it leaves from where we stood on the tick we fired, along the gun's heading that tick, and after turn k it is speed * (k - fireTime) from there (the engine's order, checked in S2's bench).
Posture
The set of subsystems that drives the robot for a tick.
PostureGate
Decides each tick whether the melee subsystems may drive (GATE-1).
PostureGate.Veto
Why melee is off for the rest of the round, or PostureGate.Veto.NONE.
PowerPolicy
When to fire full power instead of the gun's own choice.
PowerPolicy.Reason
Why a shot got the power it did: GUN when no rule applies and the gun's own power stands, POW_1 when the profile rates their gun T0, POW_2 when this battle's rolling hit rates call for full power.
ProfileCodec
The profile file format: small, hand-written, versioned and checksummed (the artifact's "Format" section).
ProfileFolder
Collects one round's observations of the opponent and folds them into its profile when the round ends (MEM-2).
ProfileFormatException
Bytes that are not a valid profile: wrong magic or version, truncated, bad checksum or bad values.
ProfileLibrary
Loads and saves opponent profiles in a ProfileStore.
ProfileLibrary.Loaded
The result of a load.
ProfileLibrary.Saved
What a save did: WRITTEN in full; WRITTEN_WITHOUT_SEEDS when only the stats fitted (MEM-5); SKIPPED when even they did not, leaving the old file; FAILED when the store or codec threw.
ProfileStore
Where opponent profiles are kept between battles: a flat directory of named byte blobs with a size quota.
Replay
Runs a recorded battle back through a fresh core and guard, the same way the robot drives them, and returns the orders for every tick (CORE-2).
Replay.Tick
One replayed tick: what the live robot issued and what the replay produced.
Report
Renders bench results as Markdown.
RobotState
A robot's position and motion at one tick: ours or the enemy's, observed, interpolated or predicted.
RobotState.Builder
Builds a RobotState; each setter returns the builder.
RobotStateLog
A robot's RobotStates keyed by tick, with linear interpolation across the ticks that were not observed.
RobotStateLog.AllStateListener
Receives each state from RobotStateLog.forAllStates(hadur2.core.model.RobotStateLog.AllStateListener).
RoundStats
Per-round counters.
Rules
The Robocode game rules the core relies on, identical to robocode.Rules.
SeedLoader
Replays an opening's seeds into the KNN views a few at a time, so that loading hundreds of samples never lands on one tick (the first scan is already the battle's slowest).
Seeds
How a KNN sample becomes a seed of OpponentProfile.SAMPLE_WIDTH shorts and back (S4).
SeedTrust
RES-4: watches one seed against the live evidence, a wave at a time.
SeedWeight
The weight a group of seeded samples carries in the KNN views (ADAPT-3).
SentryFence
Treats the sentries' border as a wall for the duel's movement (GATE-3).
ShieldDetector
SHIELD-1: watches how our bullets end and says when the enemy is shooting them down.
SimpleFormula
The simplest danger space: bullet flight time, lateral velocity and acceleration, equally weighted.
Stats
Mean and 95% confidence half-width (Student's t) of a small sample.
SurfMover
The duel's wave surfing: each tick, decides where to drive so that the enemy's next bullets are least likely to hit us, and writes the body's turn, distance and speed into the orders.
SurfMover.Mode
How to pick where to be when a wave breaks.
SurfMover.SurfOption
The three-option surf's choices; SurfMover.SurfOption.direction is the orbit sign.
Telemetry
Where the core sends telemetry lines (the artifact's CSV record format).
TickBudget
The tick budget (TIME-1, TIME-2): how much work the core may do this tick, as a computation level from 0 (everything) to TickBudget.MAX_LEVEL.
Tiers
The capability tiers a profile implies (the artifact's "Recognise, then adapt" tables), which the opening book turns into decisions at the first tick.
Tiers.Gun
How well their gun hits us: T0 (head-on or random) to T3 (a top learning gun).
Tiers.Move
How their movement holds up against our guns: M0 (predictable) to M3 (flattened surfer).
Timestamped
A sample stored in a KNN view, stamped with when it was observed.
TimestampedFiringAngle
One of the gun's KNN samples: where the enemy went relative to one of our waves, logged by GunController when the wave breaks on it (or replayed from a gun seed).
TimestampedGuessFactor
One of the surf's KNN samples: the guess factor at which an enemy wave met us, or at which one of its bullets hit us, logged by MoveController (or replayed from a surf seed).
VirtualBullet
One of the aims an opponent's recorded shot may have taken (MMOVE-3): a bullet from the shot's source along VirtualBullet.heading, flying at the shot's speed from its fire tick.
VirtualBullet.Aim
How the shooter is assumed to have aimed.
Wave
A wave: the circle a bullet fired at Wave.fireTime from Wave.sourceLocation would lie on, growing by Wave.bulletSpeed() pixels every tick.
Wave.Intersection
A range of absolute firing angles from a wave's source: a centre and a half-width.
Wave.WavePosition
Where a wave is relative to a robot, in the order a wave passes through them; see Wave.checkWavePosition(RobotState, boolean, WavePosition).
WaveManager
The waves in flight on one side of the duel, and the bookkeeping that decides when each one has passed its target.
WaveManager.AllWaveListener
Receives each wave from WaveManager.forAllWaves(hadur2.core.model.WaveManager.AllWaveListener).
WaveManager.CurrentWaveListener
Receives each wave from WaveManager.checkCurrentWaves(long, hadur2.core.model.WaveManager.CurrentWaveListener).
WaveManager.WaveBreakListener
Told when a wave has completely passed its target.
WaveMatcher
Scores the waves Hadur inferred against the bullets the enemy really fired (S2's wave fidelity).
